title: I've been building a 90s game store sim in Unity with Claude for over a month. What worked, what didn't, and a call for playtesters!
author: LittleGumbee_
selftext:
For over a month I've been making my dream game 😄 **Level '92: Video Game Store**, a cosy shop sim set in autumn 1992. You stock shelves, price games, haggle over used games and get ready for release days

It's built in Unity 6. All of the C# (about 60k lines now, gameplay plus editor tools) is written by AI coding agents: Claude Code (mostly Opus 5.5) and a little Codex. My job is direction: I wrote the brief, I make every gameplay call, I design and test all the systems, and I play every change before I accept it. I also place and adjust things in the scenes myself.

What's working so far:

\- One rulebook and a decision log. Every gameplay or design change gets a numbered entry with my exact words when I approved it.

\- Automated checks inside Unity. A batch runner plays scripted shop days, checks saves, money and stock, renders screenshots of every screen and makes a build. "It compiles" is not "it works", so nothing counts as done until it passes and I've played it.

\- Docs as the agents' memory. About 70 Markdown files in the repo, each with one job: a map of all docs, one doc per game system and maps of the code. The rule is "one fact in one place", so a session reads the map and only the two or three docs its task needs instead of the whole project.

\- Regular clean-ups instead of one big rewrite. When a doc gets near its word budget it's split by topic; when a class passes about 1500 lines it's split into partial files by area (there are over 60 now); old decisions are archived in blocks of 50. Small and often, so the context the agents read stays short and current.

What's hard:

\- Agents happily build features "for later". I have to say no a lot.

\- Art consistency. Box covers, the logo and packaging art came from ChatGPT image generation, and characters and street props from Meshy, cleaned up and rigged with Blender scripts the agents wrote. Getting them to look like one game took many rounds.

\- 3D models are the biggest weakness so far. They're passable for an early alpha, but if people have fun with the game, I'll invest in a 3D artist and an animator down the line.

\- Balance. Agents can write a simulation that plays a year of the game, but whether it's fun only a human can tell. That's why I need playtesters.

So: the first closed alpha is ready (Windows, free [itch.io](http://itch.io) key, about 1–2 hours of play plus a short survey). I'm looking for couple of playtesters of early build! If you like shop or management sims and want to try it, join the Discord.

Discord: [https://discord.gg/GkSBjrdyXP](https://discord.gg/GkSBjrdyXP)

Game page: [https://pixel-station.itch.io/level-92-video-game-store](https://pixel-station.itch.io/level-92-video-game-store)

Trailer: [https://youtu.be/rPoZo2om7qE](https://youtu.be/rPoZo2om7qE)



Happy to answer questions about the workflow: how I keep the agents on track, the Unity batch checks, or the Meshy-to-Unity pipeline.

replies.author: LittleGumbee_
replies.body: Currently don't have rain in this build, maybe in the future!

replies.author: One_Salty_Pigeon
replies.body: If you haven't might be worth looking into a plugin called Cozy Weather. Pretty nifty and I got it setup easily using Claude.

comments.author: ClashAtNightfall
comments.body: Looks fun! I was obsessed with Card Shop Simulator when it came out and this has a similar vibe. Would look at some of their patch notes for inspiration on possible things to build towards or adapt. I was extremely satisfied when they got more character models to add a sense of 'different people, more populated world' vibe.

replies.author: LittleGumbee_
replies.body: Thanks! TCG Card Shop Simulator is a big inspiration, so I'm glad the vibe comes through. Right now there are a handful of adult body types plus kids, with clothes and colours mixed for every customer, but more silhouettes are high on my list

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
Advice: Change the name of the arcade game.

Claude *loves* to use the name "Starfall" for shit. Probably about three or four of my unnamed projects have it in their Claude created name and none of them share a genre.

Also, the company logo and the cardboard cutout of that hero dude scream "AI art". Maybe work on toning that vibe down.

comments.author: I_Study_The_Patterns
comments.body: The music is very bad, I would get something that sounds 90s, not some generic YouTube background music. Otherwise looks cool.

comments.author: Kreed22vR
comments.body: This is pretty sick. Actually feels a little nostalgic. Well done, OP!

comments.author: Pleyar
comments.body: As someone who started gaming in the 90s this doesnt feel very authentic. Maybe put more effort in replicating the 90s graphic style. You can check old game magazines form the era on internet archive

comments.author: One_Salty_Pigeon
comments.body: I LOVE shop sim type games and other simulator type games and honestly this game really caught my eye. The nostalgia and vibe is just sooooo on point. I'm always picky about the graphics I like which is what makes it hard for me to like most indie dev games but this is perfect!
